correctness.rationale: For any positive net gain, stationary states are bijective with real roots of \(z=k\sin z\). On each positive sine lobe the derivative of \(z/\sin z\) changes sign once and only once because \(\sin z-z\cos z\) strictly increases. This proves every count and the \(2k/\pi+O(1)\) law without relying on finite sampling. For pure feedback the 3D return Jacobian spectrum is exactly \(\{0,0,k\cos z\}\), so strict decrease of \(z\cot z\) gives the sole stable branch in each lobe and the two exact tangency equations. A controlled \(\cot t\) expansion yields width \(2/((2m+1/2)\pi)+O(m^{-3})\); strict eigenvalues inside the unit disc ensure open three-parameter persistence. The standalone bisection code tested selected roots/widths and nonzero-feedback Schur inequalities; diagnostics are not substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The source proposes a 3D symmetric sine map emphasizing multistability, yet computes only the origin in its local equilibrium stability treatment. This result supplies a motivated complete positive-net-gain equilibrium census, proves an infinite and explicitly ordered family of opposite attracting stationary pairs, computes a sharp asymptotic width for their shrinking parameter windows, and shows that these sinks occur in open nondegenerate three-parameter regions. These are natural intrinsic dynamical invariants, not a selected tiny parameter slice or merely a scalar normalization check. It does not claim long-term chaos, attractor basins, or global stability beyond the stated domains.
